conflict_synopsis.core_view: AU 2Y is marked to a 99th-percentile hike-continuation regime while housing, labor and headline CPI already show restrictive policy biting, so receive AUD 2Y.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next Australian housing, labor or CPI print that confirms the tightening channel against a 99th-percentile 2Y.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AU labor/inflation gauges back above 50 with housing stabilizing, or a live energy-pass-through tightening trigger into a fresh AU 2Y high.

remit: underpriced easing, lower-rate repricing, or growth weakness
stance_summary: Restrictive policy is already transmitting through Australian housing, labor and disinflation while AU 2Y sits at a 99th-percentile 1y/5y extreme after a global tightening impulse. The market is pricing hike-continuation that domestic gauges do not support; receive AUD 2Y outright duration. Spot AUDUSD is the FX analog but is inferior: it is not comparably stretched, 2Y carry opposes short AUD, and AUDUSD is cheap versus copper.

catalysts: Further Australian housing-volume, stamp-duty or home-value weakness confirming the tightening channel.
AU labor remaining sub-50 (unemployment up / employment down / cooler WPI) against a 99th-percentile 2Y.
Headline or trimmed-mean CPI rolling over from 3.5%/3.6%, forcing the RBA path off the global hike-continuation narrative.
Energy-shock tail continuing to fade after the Saudi-Oman workaround, removing the imported justification for extreme AU front-end yields.
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Receive AUD 2Y outright duration (long AU 2-year government notes versus cash; research/reference RBA F2 close 4.999% as of 2026-09-16).
expression_comparison.rationale: The discrepancy lives in the AU policy path versus an extreme front-end yield, not in AUD spot. AU 2Y is at the 99.0th 1y and 99.8th 5y percentile after +39.1bp in one month, while housing transactions, unemployment and headline CPI are already softening. AUDUSD is only the 84.3rd 5y percentile (z_5y 1.23), the AU-US 2Y differential of +26bp means 2Y carry opposes short AUD, and AUDUSD trades cheap versus copper (residual z -1.33). AU-US 2Y RV is the 25.6th 1y percentile, so cross-market RV does not own the underpriced-easing gap either. Outright AU 2Y duration is the cleaner, rates-first expression.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDUSD (ECB same-fixing research/reference 0.712 as of 2026-09-18).

trade.horizon: 4-12 weeks, through the next Australian labor, CPI and housing-transaction prints
trade.invalidation: Domestic AU gauges re-accelerate with labor and inflation scores back above 50 and housing transactions stabilizing, or a renewed energy-pass-through shock that the RBA treats as a live tightening trigger while AU 2Y makes a fresh one-month high. A global duration selloff that is confirmed in AU hard data, not just imported from Fed/BoJ headlines, also kills the trade.
trade.mispricing: Pricing treats AU 2Y as a 99th-percentile tightening-continuation asset after the Fed/BoJ/energy impulse. Domestic state is already below-50 on inflation, labor and activity, with the housing channel visibly contracting. That gap is underpriced easing / lower-rate repricing in AU 2Y, not a residual FX undervaluation of AUD.
principal_risks: Energy-market shock absorbers remain weak; a second oil leg can re-import inflation and keep the RBA in the global tightening camp even with a housing slump.
Trimmed-mean CPI still 3.6% y/y and household spending had a third consecutive +1.1% m/m print, so the consumer channel is not uniformly weak.
Fed tightening bias, BoJ 1.25% and BoE 6-3 hike dissent can keep dragging G10 term yields higher and overwhelm the domestic AU housing signal.
No RBA-implied path, no positioning, and no executable broker prices are in the packet; levels stay null.
Risk-off that is stagflationary rather than a growth-scare can cheapen ACGBs instead of rallying them.
trade.structure: Outright receive AUD 2Y duration (long AU 2-year government notes versus cash). Packet yields and ECB FX are research/reference only; not an executable ticket.
trade.thesis: VERIFIED: AU 2Y closed 4.999% on 2026-09-16 (1y percentile 99.0, 5y percentile 99.8, z_1y 1.67) after +39.1bp 1m and +49.8bp 3m; AU 5Y 5.041% and AU 10Y 5.348% are likewise 99th-percentile on both windows. NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% y/y in August with transaction volumes -18% and Sydney/Melbourne home values more than 7% below peak. AU labor 47.8: unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%, employment -15.8k m/m, WPI +3.2% y/y versus +3.4% a year earlier. AU inflation 49.2: headline CPI 3.5% y/y from 3.8%, trimmed mean 3.6% unchanged. AU activity 49.2 with GDP +0.4% q/q and RBA business conditions modestly weaker; Westpac-MI sentiment then fell 5.2% to 84.4 in September. The Fed has already hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with >90% priced into the meeting; BoJ hiked to 1.25% and BoE held 6-3 with three hike votes. Desk synthesis: the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse even where domestic growth is softer. INFERENCE: AU front-end yields have been marked by that global tightening impulse to a hike-continuation regime that the housing transmission channel, labor softening and headline disinflation already contradict. Restrictive policy is biting; additional AU 2Y backup is an overpriced delay of easing, not a domestic overheating signal. AU-US 2Y at +26bp is only the 25.6th 1y percentile, so the edge is outright AU duration, not paying US versus receiving AU. UNKNOWN: RBA meeting-implied odds and reaction-function details are not in the packet; positioning/flow is unavailable; NZ official yields are unavailable; trimmed mean at 3.6% and still-positive household spending leave an energy pass-through path that could keep the RBA on hold longer than a pure housing-labor read implies.
why_now: AU 2Y, 5Y and 10Y are simultaneously at 99th-percentile 1y and 5y extremes after a 39-50bp three-month backup, coinciding with a documented housing downturn rather than hotter activity.
The Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% was >90% priced into 16 Sep and is now a known impulse; the residual is whether AU domestic gauges can justify keeping that tightening marked into ACGB 2Y.
September Westpac-MI confidence fell 5.2% to 84.4 after the housing and labor prints, a timely confirmation that the tightening channel is still biting.
Saudi ship-to-ship workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, weakening the energy-shock justification for keeping AU front-end yields at a 99th-percentile extreme.
